trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is the receipt, not a task: it unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing extra to hunt once they are done [1][2]. Plan the run in the order this guide lays out — story first, side strands before the finale, then activities, collectibles, combat and money [3][4]. Keep a manual save at the start of every chapter, because the one missable meditation in Chapter 1 cannot be replayed [3]. Expect about 200 hours in total, rated 4 out of 10 for difficulty, with most of the time going to the 100% checklist after the story [4].

steps.t: Finish the five story chapters and the finale, earning the 12 story trophies as you go.
Clear every stranger and side-character strand before the final mission, while the strands are still open.
Work through the activities, collectibles and combat trophies in stages 3 to 5, tracking your counts as you go.
Finish the 100% checklist and the money trophies in stage 6; the platinum unlocks with the last one.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players earn and it cannot be missed [1][2]. Play through the start of the game as directed — the mission teaches movement, driving and the basic controls before it asks for anything harder [3]. Follow the on-screen objectives until the mission ends, and the trophy unlocks right after the closing scene [4]. If you are checking this list before starting, there is nothing to prepare: just play the opening and it lands [2].

steps.t: Start a new game and play the opening sequence.
Follow the Gone Fishing objectives to the end.
The trophy unlocks when the mission completes.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.save: Manual save at the start of Chapter 1 — before you leave it, do the balcony meditation for trophy 28.
trophies.guide: Chapter 1 closes with this trophy, and it is unmissable as long as you keep playing the story [1][2]. The chapter sets up Lucia and Jason and the state of Leonida, and its missions are short and guided [3]. Before you finish the chapter, stop at Lucia's balcony meditation spot — it disappears once the chapter ends and there is no mission replay, so it is the one thing in Chapter 1 you can actually lose [3][4]. Then play the chapter's final mission and the trophy is yours [2].

steps.t: Play through the Chapter 1 missions in order.
Before the chapter ends, meditate at Lucia's balcony spot for the missable trophy.
Complete the chapter's final mission to unlock this trophy.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.save: Manual save at the start of Chapter 2.
trophies.guide: Chapter 2 is where the duo's partnership starts paying off, and this trophy lands when you finish its last mission [1][2]. Two partner trophies open in this chapter — losing a 4-star wanted level together and robbing three shops back-to-back — so play the partner missions with both characters available and grab those while the chapter is live [3][4]. Make a manual save at the start of the chapter, then simply work through the story missions in order until the chapter closes [3].

steps.t: Make a manual save at the start of Chapter 2.
Play the Chapter 2 missions in order, doing the partner trophies while both characters are playable.
Complete the chapter's final mission to unlock this trophy.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.save: Manual save at the start of Chapter 3 — the Yago race with its hourglass icon runs in this chapter.
trophies.guide: Chapter 3 takes the story into Vice City itself, and this trophy unlocks when its final mission is done [1][2]. This is the busiest chapter for side content: the Yago race carries an hourglass icon and is time-sensitive, and several stranger strands open here, so clear them before moving on [3][4]. The Cartel Heist mission also lands in this chapter. Make a manual save when the chapter starts, work the side strands first, then finish the story missions [3].

steps.t: Make a manual save at the start of Chapter 3.
Do the Yago race and the stranger strands that open in this chapter before they pass.
Complete the chapter's final mission to unlock this trophy.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.save: Manual save at the start of Chapter 4.
trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the last full chapter before the endgame, and this trophy unlocks when you complete it [1][2]. Three story missions in this chapter carry their own trophies — Child's Play, Headliners and the VCIA Takedown — so each one is a guaranteed unlock as you play through [3]. Bank vault robberies open up around here too, which feeds the stage 5 combat cleanup [4]. Save at the chapter start, play the missions in order, and the trophy follows the chapter's close [2].

steps.t: Make a manual save at the start of Chapter 4.
Play the Chapter 4 missions in order, earning the three mission trophies as you go.
Complete the chapter's final mission to unlock this trophy.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.save: Manual save before the final mission — after it, side strands are reported to lock.
trophies.guide: This gold trophy is the story's payoff: finish the final mission and it unlocks [1][2]. Before you start it, clear every side strand, stranger mission and partner trophy, because side content is reported to lock once the story passes it [3][4]. Sources disagree on one detail — some guides place the final mission in Chapter 4, others in Chapter 5 — so this guide lists it as the finale after Chapter 5's missions and shows both versions rather than picking one [3][4]. Make a manual save, play the finale, and the gold is yours [2].

steps.t: Finish all side strands and partner trophies before the finale — they may lock afterwards.
Make a manual save, then start the final mission.
Complete the final mission to unlock this gold trophy.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a Chapter 2 story mission, and this trophy unlocks the moment you finish it [1][2]. There is no special requirement, no hidden objective and no way to miss it — just play the story until the mission appears and complete it [3]. It is one of the early duo missions, so it also teaches how the two characters work together before the bigger partner trophies later in the chapter [4].

steps.t: Play through the Chapter 2 story until Breakfast Run appears.
Follow the mission objectives to the end.
The trophy unlocks when the mission completes.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a Chapter 3 story mission and a heist set-piece, and this trophy unlocks when you complete it [1][2]. It is unmissable — the mission is on the main story path, so every player reaches it by playing through [3]. Expect a longer, multi-stage job with driving and combat, and follow the objectives as they update [4]. There is nothing to prepare in advance; the game hands you what you need inside the mission [2].

steps.t: Play through the Chapter 3 story until The Cartel Heist appears.
Follow the heist objectives through each stage.
The trophy unlocks when the mission completes.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a Chapter 4 story mission, and this trophy unlocks when you finish it [1][2]. Like the other mission trophies it is unmissable: it sits on the main story path, so playing through Chapter 4 in order brings it to you [3]. The mission is a shorter, character-driven one, and the objectives guide you through it without any hidden requirement [4]. Just complete it and move on to the next story beat [2].

steps.t: Play through the Chapter 4 story until Child's Play appears.
Follow the mission objectives to the end.
The trophy unlocks when the mission completes.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is a Chapter 4 story mission, and this trophy unlocks when you complete it [1][2]. It is on the main story path and cannot be missed, so there is no preparation and no side requirement attached to it [3]. Play through Chapter 4's missions in order and the mission will appear; follow its objectives to the end and the trophy pops as the mission closes [4].

steps.t: Play through the Chapter 4 story until Headliners appears.
Follow the mission objectives to the end.
The trophy unlocks when the mission completes.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: The VCIA Takedown is a Chapter 4 story mission set around the airport, and this trophy unlocks when you complete it [1][2]. It is unmissable and sits on the main story path, so every player reaches it by playing Chapter 4 through [3]. The mission mixes driving and combat around the airport grounds; follow the objectives as they update and the trophy unlocks at the mission's end [4].

steps.t: Play through the Chapter 4 story until the VCIA Takedown appears.
Follow the mission objectives through the airport sequence.
The trophy unlocks when the mission completes.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a Chapter 5 story mission, and this trophy unlocks when you complete it [1][2]. It is the last named mission trophy before the finale, and it is unmissable on the main story path [3]. One note on the sources: some guides place the final mission in Chapter 4 and others in Chapter 5, so the chapter numbering around the endgame is contested — this guide follows the chapter list that puts Operation Savage Glory in Chapter 5 [3][4]. Play it through and the trophy follows [2].

steps.t: Play through the Chapter 5 story until Operation Savage Glory appears.
Follow the mission objectives to the end.
The trophy unlocks when the mission completes.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: This gold trophy is the long tail of the platinum: reach 100% completion on the in-game checklist and it unlocks [1][2]. The checklist has 14 rows — 100 optional missions, 200 of 277 vehicles scanned, 100 of 255 animals studied, 50 of 66 weapons, 70 of 80 challenges, 15 of 18 meditation spots, 300 of 397 stunts, 15 of 18 card sets, 8 bank vaults, 39 illegal operations, 42 gold shooting-range challenges, 42 drone races, 15 of Bret's target decks, and every underwater discovery [3][4]. Budget about 100 hours after the story, and use the checklist tab here to track each row [3].

steps.t: Finish the story first, then open the 100% checklist in the stats menu.
Work the checklist row by row, starting with the biggest rows: optional missions, stunts and vehicles.
Clear the counted rows that overlap other trophies — meditations, card sets, vaults and drone races.
When the checklist reads 100%, this gold trophy unlocks.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Stunts are the open-world trick jumps scattered across Leonida, and this silver trophy needs 250 of them — well short of the 397 that exist, and short of the 300 the 100% checklist wants [3][4]. Treat them as a cleanup pass after the story: drive the map with the stunt markers on, and chain nearby jumps in one route instead of hopping around at random [3]. Budget 10 to 20 hours; the harder jumps are the time sink, not the count [4]. The in-game counter tracks every completed stunt, so check it between runs [2].

steps.t: Finish the story, then turn stunt markers on and plan routes through clusters of jumps.
Complete stunts one by one, watching the in-game counter climb toward 250.
Leave the hardest jumps for last and retry them with a faster approach run.
The trophy unlocks at 250 completed stunts.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: There are 9 activity types in the game, and this trophy only asks you to try each one once — no wins, no scores, just a single attempt at each [1][2]. It is the easiest stage 3 trophy and a good first stop after the story: sampling everything also shows you which activities you enjoy before you grind the harder ones [3]. Budget 2 to 3 hours, mostly travel between activity spots [4]. Tick each type off as you try it, and the trophy lands on the ninth [2].

steps.t: Open the activities list and note the 9 types you have not tried yet.
Visit each activity spot and start it once — finishing is not required, trying is.
The trophy unlocks when all 9 types have been tried.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The shooting ranges hold 42 challenges, and this silver trophy wants a gold medal in every one of them [1][2]. It is a skill trophy, not a grind: learn each range's layout and scoring, then repeat the ones you miss until the gold threshold clears [3]. Budget 4 to 6 hours, and do it after the story when you own a full weapon set [4]. Gold in all 42 also ticks the shooting-range row of the 100% checklist, so it does double duty [3].

steps.t: Visit a shooting range and work through its challenges, learning the gold score for each.
Repeat missed challenges until each one clears gold — accuracy beats speed.
Clear all 42 challenges at gold across every range.
The trophy unlocks when the 42nd challenge turns gold.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at 14 locations, with 42 races in total across them, and this trophy needs a win at every location [3][4]. You only need one win per location, not every race, so learn each course once and move on [3]. Budget 2 to 4 hours. Winning all 42 races also fills the drone-race row of the 100% checklist, so keep racing after the trophy if you are chasing 100% [4]. The counter shows wins per location, so check it before you leave a spot [2].

steps.t: Visit each of the 14 Top Fun locations and race its course.
Win at least one race at each location — learn the course line before pushing for speed.
The trophy unlocks when all 14 locations show a win.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Leonida holds 40 races, and this trophy needs a win in 20 different ones — half the calendar [3][4]. Any 20 will do, so pick the shorter circuits and the vehicle classes you drive best, and skip the ones that fight you [3]. Budget 3 to 5 hours. Races count as different events, not repeat wins on the same course, so the tracker here counts distinct races won [2]. Do it after the story when your garage is stocked [4].

steps.t: Open the race list and pick 20 different events, favouring short circuits.
Win each chosen race once, using your best vehicle for its class.
The trophy unlocks at 20 different races won.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.missableNote: Reported time-sensitive: take the challenge when Cal offers it — it may not come back.
trophies.save: Manual save before accepting Cal's challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal offers a fishing challenge, and this trophy needs you to beat him at it [1][2]. The catch is timing: the challenge is reported to be time-sensitive, and it may not come back if you walk away from it [3][4]. Take it the first time he offers it, and make a manual save before you accept so a lost attempt costs you nothing [3]. The challenge itself is short — about 30 minutes including the fishing — and it is the only fishing trophy on the list [4].

steps.t: Make a manual save when Cal first offers the fishing challenge.
Accept the challenge at once — do not leave it for later, it may not return.
Beat Cal's score in the fishing challenge.
If you lose, reload the manual save and try again.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Arcades around Leonida hold playable games, and this trophy needs you to complete just one of them [1][2]. Pick the shortest game you can find and play it through to its end — completion is what counts, not a high score [3]. Budget about 30 minutes. It pairs naturally with the Master of None sampling pass, since the arcade is one of the 9 activity types [4].

steps.t: Find an arcade and pick its shortest game.
Play the game through to completion.
The trophy unlocks when the game ends.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missableNote: Andy's strand — finish all his missions before the finale; side strands are reported to lock once the story passes them.
trophies.save: Manual save at the start of Chapter 3; finish Andy's strand before the finale.
trophies.guide: Andy is a Lucia-only stranger in Chapter 3, and this trophy needs every mission in his strand finished, ending with his final mission [3][4]. Side strands are reported to lock once the story passes them, so do Andy's missions as soon as they appear and never leave them for after the finale [3]. Budget 2 to 3 hours. Note that Andy's strand does not count toward the 8 strands of Strangers & Freaks — it is a separate side trophy [4].

steps.t: Meet Andy in Chapter 3 as Lucia and take his first mission.
Work through his missions as each one appears.
Complete Andy's final mission before the story finale.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missableNote: Kenton's strand — finish all his missions, ending with Maritime Disputes, before the finale; side strands are reported to lock once the story passes them.
trophies.save: Manual save before starting Kenton's strand; finish it before the finale.
trophies.guide: Kenton's strand is built around shipwrecks — 7 of them — and ends with the mission Maritime Disputes [3][4]. This trophy needs the whole strand finished, so start it when it appears and work the shipwrecks as you go rather than saving them all for the end [3]. Like the other side strands it is reported to lock once the story passes it, so finish it before the finale [4]. Budget 2 to 4 hours. Kenton's strand does not count toward Strangers & Freaks [4].

steps.t: Meet Kenton and take his first mission.
Work through the strand, clearing the 7 shipwrecks as they come up.
Complete the final mission, Maritime Disputes, before the finale.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missableNote: Billy's strand — finish all his missions, ending with Hometown Heroes, before the finale; side strands are reported to lock once the story passes them.
trophies.save: Manual save at the start of Chapter 2; finish Billy's strand before the finale.
trophies.guide: Billy's strand runs through the Thrillbilly Mudclub — 5 jobs there — and ends with the mission Hometown Heroes [3][4]. This trophy needs the whole strand finished, so pick his missions up in Chapter 2 and work them as they appear [3]. Side strands are reported to lock once the story passes them, so do not leave Billy for after the finale [4]. Budget 2 to 3 hours. Billy's strand does not count toward the 8 strands of Strangers & Freaks [4].

steps.t: Meet Billy in Chapter 2 and take his first mission.
Work through his strand, doing the 5 Mudclub jobs as they appear.
Complete the final mission, Hometown Heroes, before the finale.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.missableNote: Time-sensitive: the Yago race in Chapter 3 carries an hourglass icon — miss it and the strand may not count.
trophies.save: Manual save at the start of Chapter 3 — do the Yago race the moment its hourglass appears.
trophies.guide: Eight stranger strands count toward this silver trophy, and the guides name four of them — Kirk, Kyle, Yago and Pilot Pete — with four more counting beside them [3][4]. The one to watch is Yago: his race in Chapter 3 carries an hourglass icon, which marks it time-sensitive, and missing it may cost you the strand [3]. Strands that do not count are Moses, Tyrone, Yasmani, Andy and Billy, though they carry their own trophies [4]. Budget 6 to 10 hours, and work every stranger strand you meet so the counter keeps climbing [2].

steps.t: Take every stranger mission you meet and work each strand as it appears.
In Chapter 3, do the Yago race the moment its hourglass icon appears.
Keep going until 8 counting strands are complete — Kirk, Kyle, Yago and Pilot Pete are four of them.
The trophy unlocks at 8 completed strands.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missableNote: Randy's strand — finish all his missions, and his vehicle wish list, before the finale; side strands are reported to lock once the story passes them.
trophies.save: Manual save at the start of Chapter 3; finish Randy's strand and his 16-car wish list before the finale.
trophies.guide: Randy's strand is a vehicle hunt: he wants 16 sports cars delivered, and this trophy needs his missions finished plus that wish list cleared [3][4]. Start collecting the cars as soon as his strand opens in Chapter 3 — spotting and delivering them takes longer than the missions themselves [3]. Like the other side strands it is reported to lock once the story passes it, so finish everything before the finale [4]. Budget 3 to 5 hours. Randy's strand does not count toward Strangers & Freaks [4].

steps.t: Meet Randy in Chapter 3 and take his first mission.
Deliver the 16 sports cars on his wish list as you find them.
Complete Randy's final mission before the finale.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missableNote: Tyrone's strand — finish all his missions, and the Kitty Litter Lab deliveries, before the finale; side strands are reported to lock once the story passes them.
trophies.save: Manual save at the start of Chapter 3; finish Tyrone's strand before the finale.
trophies.guide: Tyrone is a Jason-only stranger in Chapter 3, and his strand includes the Kitty Litter Lab deliveries [3][4]. This trophy needs all of his missions finished, so take them as Jason whenever they appear and keep the deliveries moving [3]. Side strands are reported to lock once the story passes them, so finish Tyrone's strand before the finale [4]. Budget 2 to 3 hours. His strand does not count toward the 8 strands of Strangers & Freaks [4].

steps.t: Meet Tyrone in Chapter 3 as Jason and take his first mission.
Work through his missions, doing the Kitty Litter Lab deliveries as they come up.
Complete Tyrone's final mission before the finale.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.missableNote: THE missable trophy: Lucia's balcony meditation in Chapter 1 disappears after that chapter, and the game has no mission replay. Keep a manual save at the start of every chapter.
trophies.save: Manual save at the start of Chapter 1 — meditate on Lucia's balcony BEFORE finishing the chapter.
trophies.guide: This is the one trophy that can genuinely be missed: Lucia's balcony meditation in Chapter 1 disappears after that chapter, and the game has no mission replay, so a player who finishes Chapter 1 without it has no way back except an old save [3][4]. There are 18 meditation spots across Leonida, and you need every one of them [1][2]. Sources disagree on the count that matters — some guides say 18 spots, others say 15 count for the 100% checklist — so this guide shows both: meditate at all 18, and the 100% row needs 15 of them [3][4]. Do the balcony spot first, in Chapter 1, then sweep the rest [3].

steps.t: At the start of Chapter 1, make a manual save, then meditate at Lucia's balcony spot before the chapter ends.
Visit the remaining meditation spots across Leonida, tracking them on the counter.
Meditate at all 18 spots — the 100% checklist counts 15 of them, but the trophy wants every one.
The trophy unlocks at the 18th spot.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.missableNote: Time-sensitive: a Jason-only strand — start it when it appears and finish it before the finale.
trophies.save: Manual save when Bret's strand appears; finish it before the finale.
trophies.guide: Bret wants a unique animal hunted, and this trophy is the end of his Jason-only strand [3][4]. Start the strand when it appears in Chapter 2 and finish it before the finale, because side strands are reported to lock once the story passes them [3]. No launch-day method is confirmed for which animal or where the hunt triggers — the guides agree on the strand and the Jason-only condition, but not on the hunt itself — so this trophy carries an unconfirmed badge in this guide and no invented steps [4]. Bret also has 15 target decks to clear for the 100% checklist, which is a separate, counted task [3].

steps.t: Meet Bret in Chapter 2 as Jason and take his first mission.
Work through his strand as the missions appear.
Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for — the exact animal and trigger are not yet confirmed in the launch guides, so check the sources linked here before you go.
Complete Bret's final mission before the finale.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Leonida hides 18 collectible card sets, and this silver trophy needs just 3 of them completed [3][4]. It is a gentle start to the card hunt: pick the sets whose cards cluster in one area and finish those first [3]. Budget 4 to 8 hours. The 100% checklist wants 15 of the 18 sets, so the full hunt is much longer than this trophy — but this silver lands early and shows you how the cards are spread [4]. Track sets, not single cards, and the counter moves when a set completes [2].

steps.t: Pick three card sets whose cards cluster in one area.
Collect every card in the first set, then the second, then the third.
The trophy unlocks when the third set completes.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK spots are the photo locations scattered across Leonida, and this silver trophy needs 100 of them [1][2]. The guides break the count down by region — 31, 35 and 23 across the three areas they list — so plan your sweep region by region instead of wandering [3][4]. Budget 6 to 10 hours, mostly travel. Each WAiNK counts when the photo registers at the spot, so watch the counter and do not leave a region until its number matches the guide [3].

steps.t: Sweep the first region's WAiNK spots, watching the counter climb.
Move to the next region and repeat until the regional counts match the guide.
The trophy unlocks at 100 WAiNK locations.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: The game holds 80 challenges in 8 sets of 10, and this trophy needs 50 of them done [3][4]. Most players earn it along the way without trying, because challenges cover driving, combat and exploration and tick off during normal play [3]. If you want it faster, open the challenge list after the story and clear the easy sets first — the ones tied to things you already do [4]. The 100% checklist wants 70 of the 80, so this trophy is a waypoint on that longer road [3].

steps.t: Play normally — challenges complete during story, activities and exploration.
After the story, open the challenge list and clear the easiest unfinished sets.
The trophy unlocks at 50 completed challenges.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missableNote: Needs Jason and Lucia together — do it while both are playable and partnered.
trophies.save: Manual save before raising your wanted level; do it in Chapter 2 while partnered.
trophies.guide: This trophy needs Jason and Lucia together: build a 4-star wanted level with your partner beside you, then lose the heat and escape [1][2]. It only works while both are playable and partnered, so do it in Chapter 2 when the duo missions put you together — waiting for later risks finding them apart [3][4]. Some guides flag it as missable and others treat it as repeatable, so this guide lists it under disagreement and says plainly: do it at the first good chance [3][4]. Make a manual save first, then raise the heat and break away [3].

steps.t: Make a manual save while Jason and Lucia are partnered in Chapter 2.
Raise your wanted level to 4 stars with your partner beside you.
Break line of sight and escape until the wanted level clears.
The trophy unlocks when the heat is lost with your partner present.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missableNote: Opens after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break — needs Jason and Lucia together, so do it while both are playable and partnered.
trophies.save: Manual save after the Coffee Break mission; do it while partnered.
trophies.guide: This trophy opens after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, and it needs three shop robberies back-to-back with your partner, without ever losing your wanted level in between [3][4]. Jason and Lucia must be together, so do it while both are playable and partnered — the window is Chapter 2 [3]. Some guides flag it missable and others treat it as repeatable, so this guide lists it under disagreement and advises doing it at the first chance [4]. Plan a route with three close shops, keep the heat on, and do not stop between robberies [3].

steps.t: Complete the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, then make a manual save.
Pick three shops close together and rob the first with your partner beside you.
Rob the second and third back-to-back without losing your wanted level.
The trophy unlocks after the third robbery.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Leonida's roads hold 277 base-model vehicles, and this trophy needs you to discover 100 of them [3][4]. Discovery happens as you encounter new vehicles, so most of it comes free during the story and the side strands [3]. The 100% checklist wants 200 of the 277 scanned, so this trophy is the halfway mark on a longer hunt [4]. After the story, sweep the map's traffic hotspots and car parks for the models you have not seen yet [3].

steps.t: Play the story and side strands — new vehicles count as you meet them.
After the story, sweep traffic hotspots and car parks for unseen models.
The trophy unlocks at 100 vehicles discovered.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus slows the fight down, and this trophy needs 5 enemies taken down inside a single use of it [1][2]. The trick is picking a crowded fight: wait until five enemies are in front of you, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them before it ends [3]. Budget about 15 minutes once you find the right spot — a busy shootout or a gang hideout works best [4]. If you only get four, reload the moment and try a denser group [3].

steps.t: Find a crowded fight with at least five enemies in front of you.
Trigger Combat Focus and take down five enemies before it ends.
The trophy unlocks on the fifth takedown in that single use.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableNote: A one-off setup — save before you try it; a failed attempt means re-planning the approach.
trophies.guide: VCIA is the airport, and this trophy wants an unscheduled departure from it — getting a plane out without going through the normal channels [3][4]. It is a one-off setup, so make a manual save before you enter the airport grounds [3]. Some guides flag it missable and others treat it as repeatable, so this guide lists it under disagreement and advises saving first and planning the approach before you move [4]. Budget about 30 minutes including the setup [2].

steps.t: Make a manual save before entering VCIA.
Get to a plane on the airfield and prepare your departure route.
Make the unscheduled departure from VCIA.
If it fails, reload the save and re-plan the approach.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Rhinos are the tanks of Leonida, and this trophy is about spending time in one — the description itself is the hint [1][2]. Get into a Rhino and use it: drive it, take the heat that comes with it, and the trophy follows from the ride [3]. It is not missable and not timed, so grab it whenever a Rhino crosses your path after the story [4]. Budget about 30 minutes from finding the tank to the unlock [2].

steps.t: Find a Rhino tank after the story.
Get in and drive it, taking on the attention it draws.
The trophy unlocks from the ride.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.missableNote: Needs the Snap Gun from a Chapter 3 mission — do the robbery undetected; if spotted, reload the save.
trophies.save: Manual save before the robbery; reload if you are spotted.
trophies.guide: This trophy needs a jewelry store robbery with nobody spotting you, and it needs the Snap Gun, which comes from a Chapter 3 mission — so it cannot be done before that mission [3][4]. Plan the robbery, make a manual save outside the store, and go in quiet [3]. Some guides flag it missable and others treat it as repeatable, so this guide lists it under disagreement: either way, a spotted attempt costs you only a reload [4]. Budget 1 to 2 hours including the setup [2].

steps.t: Complete the Chapter 3 mission that gives you the Snap Gun.
Make a manual save outside a jewelry store and plan a quiet route in.
Rob the store without being detected.
If you are spotted, reload the save and try again.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Bank vaults open up in the later chapters, and this silver trophy needs 5 of them robbed with a clean escape each time [1][2]. The count is where the sources disagree: this trophy wants 5 vaults, but the 100% checklist wants 8 vaults robbed, and some guides count 22 bank jobs in total — so this guide shows all three numbers rather than hiding the conflict [3][4]. Budget 2 to 4 hours. Rob 5 for the trophy, then keep going to 8 for the checklist [3].

steps.t: Unlock bank vault robberies in the later chapters.
Rob a vault and escape cleanly, then repeat.
The trophy unlocks at 5 vaults robbed and escaped.
Keep going to 8 vaults for the 100% checklist row.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks run routes across Leonida, and this trophy needs one robbed with a clean escape [1][2]. Watch a route, stop the truck, take the cash and break away before the response arrives [3]. It is one of the quickest stage 5 trophies — about 30 minutes from spotting a truck to the unlock [4]. It is not missable, so do it whenever a truck crosses your path [2].

steps.t: Find an armored truck on its route.
Stop the truck and rob it.
Escape cleanly to unlock the trophy.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Leonida is the whole state, and this trophy needs every part of it explored — 52 areas on the counter [3][4]. Most of it happens naturally: the story and the side strands drag you across the map, and the remaining pockets are quick drives [3]. Budget 2 to 4 hours for the cleanup pass after the story. It pairs well with the vehicle and WAiNK sweeps, since all three want you driving the same roads [4]. The counter shows explored areas, so check it before you call a region done [2].

steps.t: Play the story and side strands — they cover most of the map.
After the story, drive the remaining areas until the counter shows them explored.
The trophy unlocks when all 52 areas are explored.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Every gang in Leonida runs illegal operations, and this trophy needs one robbed from each of the 9 gangs [1][2]. The operations are spread across the map, so treat it as a sweep: clear one gang's operation, then move to the next gang's territory [3]. Budget 3 to 5 hours. The 100% checklist wants all 39 illegal operations robbed, so this trophy is the first pass on a much longer cleanup [4]. Watch the gang counter so you do not rob the same gang twice [2].

steps.t: Find an illegal operation belonging to a gang you have not robbed yet.
Rob the operation and escape.
Repeat for each of the 9 gangs until every gang shows robbed.
The trophy unlocks when the 9th gang's operation is robbed.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: This trophy is UNCONFIRMED: no launch-day method exists for it, so this guide invents no steps for it [1][2]. The official description points at a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach, which suggests a quiet moment at a beach bar rather than a mission [5]. What is not yet known is which spot, which drink, or whether a character or time of day matters — the guides list the trophy but give no working method [1]. Check the sources linked here for updates, and do not trust any walkthrough that claims a confirmed route without one [2].

steps.t: No confirmed steps exist yet — the launch guides list the trophy with no working method.
The description points to Ocean Beach; visit its bars and viewpoints once the method is confirmed.
Check the linked sources for a confirmed method before spending time on it.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missableNote: A one-off smash — save before you try it; a failed run means finding another showroom.
trophies.save: Manual save before entering the showroom.
trophies.guide: This trophy is UNCONFIRMED and flagged missable: the description wants you to smash your way out of a vehicle showroom, and a failed run means finding another showroom [1][5]. No launch-day method is confirmed — which showroom, which vehicle, or what counts as the smash are all still open [2]. Make a manual save before you try any showroom, because the one-off nature of the attempt is the one thing the guides do agree on [5]. Check the linked sources for a confirmed method before you commit to a run [1].

steps.t: Make a manual save before entering any vehicle showroom.
No confirmed method exists yet for which showroom or vehicle counts.
Check the linked sources for a confirmed method, then attempt the smash and reload the save if it fails.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: The Kolt & Associates bowling alley holds this trophy, and the description's word is follow-through — a full bowling visit, played properly [1][2]. Go to the alley in Chapter 2 or later, play through a game, and follow through on your throws [3]. Budget about an hour. It is a hidden trophy on PlayStation, so it stays masked here until you earn it or reveal it [2]. Bowling also feeds the activity sampling for Master of None [4].

steps.t: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Play a full game of bowling with proper follow-through on your throws.
The trophy unlocks when the visit completes.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This trophy carries a reported lead only, not a confirmed method: the description points at a partnership with mass appeal, and the lead in the guides is to raise Strength to the maximum for both characters [3][4]. That is a lead, not a verified route — the guides report it, none of them confirms it in the game [4]. Budget 3 to 5 hours of training if you follow the lead, and treat it as a stage 6 cleanup task [3]. If the lead proves wrong, the sources linked here are where a confirmed method will appear first [2].

steps.t: Train Strength for both Jason and Lucia toward the maximum.
Keep training until both characters reach max Strength.
The lead says the trophy follows from max Strength on both characters — it is reported, not confirmed.
If it does not unlock, check the linked sources for a confirmed method.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: The game tracks the choices you make across the story — 500 tracked choice moments on the counter — and this trophy follows from playing through them [1][2]. There is no single choice to hunt and no way to miss it: keep playing, keep deciding, and the counter climbs as the story moves [3]. It lands along the way in stage 6 for most players, once the story's decisions have piled up [4]. If it has not popped by the finale, finish the remaining story beats and it follows [2].

steps.t: Play the story and make choices as they come — every decision counts.
Keep going through the chapters; the counter climbs with each choice.
The trophy unlocks once the tracked choices reach their mark.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: This trophy is UNCONFIRMED: no launch-day method exists for it, so this guide invents no steps for it [1][2]. The description hints at a second attempt succeeding where the first failed — a retry of some kind — but the guides do not agree on what, and none of them gives a working method [5]. It may connect to a retryable activity or a second visit somewhere, but that is a guess, and this guide does not present guesses as method [1]. Check the sources linked here for a confirmed method [2].

steps.t: No confirmed steps exist yet — the launch guides list the trophy with no working method.
The description suggests a second attempt succeeding; what it applies to is not yet confirmed.
Check the linked sources for a confirmed method before spending time on it.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: This trophy is UNCONFIRMED: no launch-day method exists for it, so this guide invents no steps for it [1][2]. The description reads like a reaction to something strange — the kind of line that fits a hidden event or an odd encounter somewhere in Leonida [5]. Which event, where it happens, or what triggers it is not yet confirmed in any launch guide [1]. Check the sources linked here for a confirmed method, and ignore any walkthrough that claims a route without one [2].

steps.t: No confirmed steps exist yet — the launch guides list the trophy with no working method.
The description suggests a strange hidden event; its trigger is not yet confirmed.
Check the linked sources for a confirmed method before spending time on it.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: This trophy is UNCONFIRMED: no launch-day method exists for it, so this guide invents no steps for it [1][2]. The description mixes bowling with a melee drive-by — knocking targets over from a moving vehicle with a melee attack — but the guides do not say where, against whom, or how many targets count [5]. It may connect to the bowling alley, but that is a guess, and this guide does not present guesses as method [1]. Check the sources linked here for a confirmed method [2].

steps.t: No confirmed steps exist yet — the launch guides list the trophy with no working method.
The description suggests a melee drive-by that bowls targets over; the details are not yet confirmed.
Check the linked sources for a confirmed method before spending time on it.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills come from the bigger scores, and this trophy needs $250,000 of them laundered through your contacts [1][2]. It builds along the way: every heist and vault job adds marked cash, and laundering it through contacts turns it clean [3]. Do not rush it — by the time the story is done and the stage 5 vaults are cleared, the counter is usually most of the way there [4]. Keep laundering after every score and the trophy lands in stage 6 [3].

steps.t: Earn Marked Bills from heists and vault robberies.
Launder the bills through your contacts after each score.
Keep laundering until the counter reaches $250,000.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: This trophy counts every dollar you spend across all shops, and it needs $100,000 of it [1][2]. It is the easiest economy trophy: weapons, clothes, cars and supplies all count, and normal play covers much of the total before the story ends [3]. If it has not popped by stage 6, buy the big-ticket items you still want — a car or a weapon set — and the counter finishes quickly [4]. There is no trick to it, just spending [2].

steps.t: Buy weapons, clothes, cars and supplies as you play — all shops count.
Watch the counter climb toward $100,000.
In stage 6, buy any big-ticket items you still want to finish the total.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: There are 8 garage properties to buy, and this trophy needs all of them [1][2]. Garages open up from Chapter 2, and each one is a simple purchase once you have the cash [3]. Budget about 15 minutes once you can afford them — the buying itself is quick, the money is the only gate [4]. It also feeds the spending counter for Treat Yo Self, so the two trophies move together [3].

steps.t: Save up enough cash for the garage properties.
Buy each of the 8 garages as you can afford them.
The trophy unlocks when the 8th garage is purchased.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: The Scooter Bros app takes vehicle registrations, and this trophy needs 10 vehicles registered to it [1][2]. It opens in Chapter 2, and the work is simple: find a vehicle, register it in the app, and repeat [3]. Budget 1 to 2 hours, mostly finding ten different vehicles worth registering [4]. It pairs with the vehicle discovery sweep for Whip It Good, since both want you meeting new vehicles [3].

steps.t: Open the Scooter Bros app from Chapter 2 onward.
Find a vehicle and register it to the app.
Repeat until 10 vehicles are registered.
